title: Trader Joe's coupon policy: the chain issues no coupons of its own
publisher: Trader Joe's (quoted via third-party reporting; the retailer's own page was not retrieved in this pass)
offer_text: "We have low prices, every day. NO coupons. NO membership cards. NO discounts. NO glitzy promotions or couponing wars at our stores. We offer the best everyday values, every day." Separately, a Trader Joe's public relations manager (Nakia Rohde) is quoted as saying: "We do not offer Trader Joe's coupons. We stay focused on providing the best everyday values, every day. However, we do accept manufacturer's coupons for other brand's products we carry."

bay_area.note: Trader Joe's operates many stores across the nine Bay Area counties. The practical consequence for Bay Area shoppers: do not look for Trader Joe's coupons, but a manufacturer coupon for a name-brand item the store carries may be honoured at the register.

title: How social media was used in this research pass (and why no offer is sourced from it)
offer_text: Method note: social platforms were searched for leads only. No offer in this dataset cites Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok or any other social platform as its source of truth.

findings.facebook_instagram: Brand coupon posts on Facebook and Instagram sit behind authentication walls and are not retrievable by an anonymous crawler, so no Facebook or Instagram post could be read and therefore none is cited. Re-tested in pass 6 (2026-09-22): an anonymous fetch of https://www.instagram.com/target/ returned HTTP 403 — the wall is confirmed live, not assumed. Where a brand runs a social-only offer, the only defensible citation is the brand's own website or app, which is what this dataset uses.
findings.reddit: Reddit was used strictly as a lead generator. The only substantive lead taken from it was the Costco Instant Savings book cycle dates, which are recorded in the excluded list as plausible-but-unofficial and are NOT used to date any offer. Reddit threads also surfaced the getpgoffer.com P&G/Costco rebate, which was then verified directly on the official P&G microsite and IS included.
findings.tiktok: A TikTok embed appeared in retrieved content from a coupon-media page. No TikTok content was read or cited.

sources.title: r/Costco
sources.evidence: Used to locate the getpgoffer.com rebate lead and the Instant Savings cycle dates. Both leads were then checked: getpgoffer.com was verified as official P&G and included; the cycle dates could not be verified against Costco and were excluded.

checks: Confirmed that no entry in data/entries cites a social platform as its only source
Every social-media-derived lead is either verified against an official domain or recorded in the excluded list
Pass 6 re-test: anonymous fetch of instagram.com/target returned HTTP 403, confirming zero anonymous readability persists

flags.detail: Because Facebook and Instagram cannot be crawled anonymously, genuinely social-only offers (e.g. a Bay Area restaurant's Instagram-only happy-hour code) are invisible to this dataset. Closing this gap needs either an authenticated session or a manual review workflow — both are listed in ROADMAP.md.

Social platforms are the dominant distribution channel for fake coupons and gift-card giveaways (Trader Joe's, Costco, Kroger and similar). Treating a social post as a source would import that risk directly, which is why the rule is: leads yes, citations no.

title: Colgate: official site states coupons are temporarily unavailable (while a Colgate microsite advertises printables)
offer_text: "Special Offers — Coupons Temporarily Unavailable. We're updating our online coupon experience. During this time, coupons are unavailable on our website. Thank you for your patience as we work behind the scenes. Please check back soon for updated offers." — fetched live 2026-09-22 (full page, single chunk, nothing truncated). The same day, a search index showed smiles.colgate.com/page/content/special-offers titled "Colgate® Coupons, Printable Coupons" promising "Print coupons for your favorite Colgate® oral care products"; a direct fetch of that microsite failed twice on the verification date, so the contradiction is recorded rather than resolved. Pass 4 (2026-09-22, later): the main page was re-fetched and printed the identical text; the microsite failed again on both the offers path and the domain root, and a pass-4 search for the microsite returned no result from smiles.colgate.com at all — its coupon advertisement now stands on the pass-1 snippet only. Pass 5 (2026-09-22, later still): the main page was fetched a third time and printed the identical text again — "Coupons Temporarily Unavailable / We're updating our online coupon experience. / During this time, coupons are unavailable on our website. / Thank you for your patience as we work behind the scenes. / Please check back soon for updated offers." A fifth retrieval attempt on smiles.colgate.com failed in this pass too (the retrieval proxy returned a signature error rather than page content, which is a retrieval failure, not evidence about the site), and a targeted search for the microsite returned only colgate.com's "Coupons Temporarily Unavailable" page. The contradiction is therefore still unresolved after five attempts across three passes, and the main site's suspension notice remains the only actively served official Colgate coupon text.
expiry_basis: Point-in-time state of the issuer's page.

bay_area.note: Applies nationally, including all Bay Area retailers that would honour Colgate manufacturer coupons.

sources.title: Special Offers | Colgate®
sources.evidence: Full page retrieved live on 2026-09-22 and again in pass 4 the same day — identical body text both times, quoted verbatim in offer_text, including 'Coupons Temporarily Unavailable' and 'Please check back soon for updated offers'. Pass 5 (2026-09-22): third full live fetch of this URL; body text byte-identical to passes 1 and 4, including the heading "Coupons Temporarily Unavailable" and the closing "Please check back soon for updated offers".

sources.evidence: Search snippet only: "Print coupons for your favorite Colgate® oral care products. Find coupons for toothpastes, teeth whitening products, and much more." Live fetch failed on 2026-09-22 (proxy error), and an older colgate.com result (Step2.vsp form) references a 2009 'spend $15 / free travel bag' mail-in — a relic, not a current offer. Pass 4 (same date): two further direct fetches failed (the offers path and the domain root), and a targeted search for "smiles.colgate.com special offers" returned no organic result from that domain — only aggregator 'Colgate promo code' pages and an India-market Smiles Club terms page. Pass 5 (same date): a fifth retrieval attempt on this microsite failed (proxy signature error, i.e. no page content obtained), and a pass-5 search for Colgate coupons returned only the main-site suspension page — no organic result from smiles.colgate.com. The microsite's printable-coupon claim still rests on the pass-1 snippet alone.

Contradicting microsite snippet recorded with its failed-retrieval note rather than silently dropped

Pass 4 re-verification (2026-09-22): main page re-fetched — byte-identical statement; microsite unreachable via two further fetch attempts and absent from that day's search results, so the 'temporarily unavailable' statement remains the only actively served official text

The contradicting page is evidenced only by a search snippet because two live fetches failed on the verification date.

title: P&G brandSAVER publishes its own retailer acceptance list — eight retailers, of which only CVS was confirmed in the Bay Area
offer_text: The issuer's coupon page answers the question directly: "Which retailers accept brandSAVER™ coupons? brandSAVER™ coupons are accepted at the following retailers–and we're working on adding more! CVS / Discount Drug Mart / Dorothy Lane Market / Food Depot / Hartig Drug Stores / Lagree's Food Stores / Other Avenues Coop / Western Drug Store". The same page publishes the redemption flow: "1 Create a P&G brandSAVER™ Account / 2 Download Coupon24 and set up a Coupon24 account. / 3 Link your Coupon24 account to your brandSAVER™ account. / 4 Send your brandSAVER™ coupons to the Coupon24 app. / 5 Use your app to scan your digital coupons at checkout. Voilà!", and states "brandSAVER™ digital coupons are accessible to all P&G brandSAVER™ members and once selected, are sent to the Coupons24 app to be used at participating retailers. Just scan the QR code when you're checking out to start saving in-store!" On the phone requirement: "For security reasons, brandSAVER™ coupons can only be accessed through one verified phone number per account."
expiry_basis: Point-in-time state of the issuer's page, read on 2026-09-22.

bay_area.note: Applies to every P&G brandSAVER digital coupon in this dataset (112 entries as of pass 5). Of the eight retailers the issuer names, CVS is the one whose Bay Area store presence this project has already verified elsewhere in the dataset; the other seven could not be confirmed as operating inside the nine-county Bay Area during this pass and no Bay Area presence is asserted for them. A Bay Area shopper without a CVS nearby may have no in-range redemption point for these coupons at all.

sources.title: Save $100s on brands you love with our digital coupons | P&G brandSAVER™
sources.evidence: The "Frequently asked questions" and "How to use" sections were retrieved live in pass 5 (the same fetch cycle that harvested all 112 coupon rows). Quoted verbatim in offer_text: the eight-retailer acceptance list, the five-step Coupon24 flow including "Use your app to scan your digital coupons at checkout. Voilà!", the "Just scan the QR code when you're checking out to start saving in-store!" sentence, and the one-verified-phone-number-per-account rule. The page also states "What are brandSAVER™ coupons? brandSAVER™ digital coupons are accessible to all P&G brandSAVER™ members and once selected, are sent to the Coupons24 app to be used at participating retailers."

sources.evidence: Retrieved as a search result from P&G's own care hub: "For the digital brandSAVER coupons, follow these steps: Browse the available coupons on the P&G brandSAVER site. Download Coupon24 and set up a Coupon24 account. Enjoy savings with digital brandSAVER coupons! Send your brandSAVER coupons to the Coupon24 app. *Note: there is a 20 coupon limit. Once a coupon is chosen to 'put in the basket' a pop up appears and states: 'Add up to 20 coupons to your basket, go to your basket and send to your Coupon24 app!'" The 20-coupon basket cap is therefore the issuer's own stated limit, not an assumption.

checks: Retailer acceptance list read verbatim from the issuer's own FAQ, in the same fetch cycle as the 112 coupon rows
Five-step redemption flow read verbatim from the same page (the 'How to use' section)
Basket cap corroborated on a second P&G-operated property (its consumer care hub)
The earlier, broader retailer claim in this dataset was located, compared against the issuer's list and corrected rather than left in place

flags.detail: Correction made in pass 5 (2026-09-22). Passes 1-4 recorded on all 36 then-existing P&G entries that these coupons are redeemable "at participating U.S. retailers that accept P&G brandSAVER digital coupons, which include Bay Area Safeway, Lucky, Andronico's Community Markets, CVS, Walgreens, Target and Walmart stores". The issuer's own published acceptance list contains none of Safeway, Lucky, Andronico's, Walgreens, Target or Walmart — only CVS overlaps. The unsupported claim was removed, confidence on every P&G entry was lowered from high to medium, the locator on every P&G entry was repointed from a Safeway locator to a CVS locator, and each entry now carries a retailer-list-published warning naming all eight retailers. The 112 coupons themselves are unaffected: their text, values and printed expiries were all read from the same official page and re-confirmed in pass 5.

Redemption runs through a third-party app: the issuer's steps require downloading Coupon24, creating a Coupon24 account, linking it to the brandSAVER account and scanning a QR code at checkout. A shopper without a smartphone, or whose store's lanes do not support the scan, cannot use these coupons even where the retailer participates.

P&G's care hub states there is a 20-coupon limit per basket ("Add up to 20 coupons to your basket, go to your basket and send to your Coupon24 app!"). With 112 coupons published on the page at the verification date, a single trip cannot carry the whole slate.

"For security reasons, brandSAVER™ coupons can only be accessed through one verified phone number per account." The issuer also discloses that using the service consents to collection of consumer health data under the P&G Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy, with withdrawal available through P&G's Consumer Health Data Preference Center.

title: Dollar Tree accepts manufacturer coupons in-store — rules that matter at the register (published policy)
offer_text: In-Store Coupon Acceptance Policy (official): accepts manufacturer coupons only (no competitor coupons); one coupon per item; up to four identical coupons per customer per day; up to two internet-printed coupons per customer per day (must have a valid expiry and a remit address); no photocopies; no cash back on overage (value reduced to item price); 'free item' coupons only accepted for buy-one-get-one styles with a purchase requirement; tax paid by the customer.
expiry_basis: Standing published policy; no end date.

bay_area.note: Why it matters: Dollar Tree sells many items above $1.25 now, and its stores accept the manufacturers' coupons indexed in this dataset (P&G, Kellanova, Coupons.com printables) subject to these rules — a real redemption outlet across the nine-county area (official store-directory pages confirm coupon acceptance per store).

sources.title: Terms and Conditions — In-Store Coupon Acceptance Policy
sources.evidence: "We accept Manufacturer Coupons only. We do not accept retail-specific coupons... We accept up to four of the same Manufacturer Coupons per customer per day... We accept up to two Internet Coupons per customer per day... We will not give cash back if the face value of a Manufacturer Coupon is greater than the purchase price of the Item... Manufacturer Coupons for free Items are only accepted if a purchase is required to get one free."

sources.title: Dollar Tree stores — California directory
sources.evidence: Each official store page carries the FAQ: "Yes, we accept coupons in our stores. Please visit our Terms & Conditions page to view our In-Store Coupon Acceptance Policy. At this time, we cannot accept coupons online."

Rules transcribed as a summary here; the governing text is the linked T&C page

title: Grocery Outlet and manufacturer coupons — what could and couldn't be verified
offer_text: Level-C policy note: Grocery Outlet publishes no manufacturer-coupon acceptance policy on its official site (groceryoutlet.com/faqs returns a CAPTCHA-gated shell; no policy text). Third-party sources consistently report the chain does NOT accept manufacturer coupons — an r/GroceryOutlet thread citing a store owner, The Krazy Coupon Lady's store guide, and a third-party deals blog all state the opportunistic-buy inventory model blocks coupon redemption because reimbursement can't be processed. Grocery Outlet DOES run its own issuer coupons (WOW alerts $3-off-$25 signup offer, in the dataset as its own entry) — do not confuse the two.

bay_area.note: Grocery Outlet has dozens of Bay Area stores (it is Emeryville-headquartered); shoppers should assume manufacturer coupons from this dataset will NOT scan there and plan redemptions at the chains listed on those coupons instead.

sources.title: Wow Alerts — Grocery Outlet (official)
sources.evidence: "New email sign-ups receive a coupon for $3 off a $25 purchase!" — proves the issuer runs its own store coupons even though no manufacturer-coupon policy page could be located on the official domain.

sources.title: Does Grocery Outlet accept coupons? — r/GroceryOutlet
sources.publisher: Reddit (community; includes a user identifying as a GO owner)
sources.evidence: Thread answer attributed to a store owner: Grocery Outlet does not accept manufacturer coupons; the opportunistic-buy model prevents redemption. NOT official evidence — recorded as the strongest third-party signal.

sources.title: Grocery Outlet store guide
sources.evidence: Store guide notes Grocery Outlet does not accept manufacturer coupons while WOW email alerts occasionally carry store coupons like $5 off — consistent with the issuer's own $3-off-$25 signup page.

Three independent third-party sources agree on non-acceptance; recorded as level C because the issuer itself could not be quoted
The issuer's OWN coupon channel (WOW alerts) is verified separately and indexed as an entry, so this note must not be read as 'no GO coupons exist'

Grocery Outlet stores are independently owned and operated; acceptance can vary by location even where a pattern is reported.

title: Hobby Lobby's famous '40% off one item' coupon is sunset — today's model is standing 40%-off departments
offer_text: Scam-watch/policy note: coupon sites still list a Hobby Lobby '40% off one regular-priced item' weekly coupon. The issuer's current site offers no such coupon, and hasn't for years — a 2019 cached copy of hobbylobby.com is the most recent official evidence of that coupon's existence. Instead, Hobby Lobby now runs standing department pricing: Home Decor, Party, Frames, Books and more are 'Always 40% Off The Marked Price' (with rotating weekly-ad categories), so '40% off one item' would be strictly worse than the current model on most baskets. Treat circulating weekly 40%-off-one-item coupons as stale.

bay_area.note: Hobby Lobby operates stores serving the Bay Area (Store Finder on the official site); the standing department discounts apply automatically at the register.

sources.title: Hobby Lobby Arts & Crafts Store (home page)
sources.evidence: Current home page shows standing pricing: "40%off Home Decor — Always 40% Off The Marked Price* ... Party ... Always 40% Off The Marked Price* ... Discounts Valid Online & In-Store" — no single-item weekly coupon anywhere on the landing surface.

sources.title: Shop Our Weekly Ad — Hobby Lobby
sources.evidence: Weekly-ad page repeats "**Always 40% off the Marked Price***" across departments with printed exclusions ('Seasonal Department', items labeled Kitchen, Bath, Closet, Gift or 'Your Price') — again with no general-item coupon.

sources.title: Hobby Lobby (cached copy from April 2019)
sources.publisher: Hobby Lobby (historical cache of the official page)
sources.evidence: The 2019 cached page shows the discontinued coupon: "40% off one item at regular price — Get Coupon ... Limit one coupon per customer per day ... Offer is not valid with any other coupon, discount or previous purchase." This is the last official evidence of the coupon; current pages no longer carry it.

checks: Both current official pages (home + weekly ad) carry only standing department pricing and no single-item coupon
The discontinued coupon's exact 2019 wording retrieved from a cached copy of the SAME official domain, documenting the before/after
Discontinuation is an inference from the issuer's own current pages plus the dated cache — flagged as inference, not presented as an issuer announcement

'Always 40% off the marked price' is shelf pricing by department, not a coupon; comparisons to old coupon value should note the marked-price basis.
